newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends at day's lows after NY falters.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends at day's lows after NY falters.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures ended at session lows after surrendering mid-afternoon gains as an early rally in New York proved shortlived, traders said.
The benchmark March contract finished $7 down at $1,228 a tonne, but good buying was seen at the lows. It had earlier touched a high of $1,244, driven by the rally in New York.
The contract was due $20 up but only managed to gap $5 higher at the open. Renewed origin selling notably from Vietnam soon led prices into the minus column.
Technically, the second-month position faces stiff support at $1,225.
Traders said in the absence of fresh fundamental news at the start of 1997, the attention centred on the New York arabica futures.
New York's benchmark March contract strolled past the closely-watched 117.50 cents a lb barrier, the peak seen in the previous three straight trading days, to a high of 119.20 on fund buying.
But it soon lost ground and moved back to around 116 at midsession on trade profit-taking.
"But we hope to see the market close above 117.50," said one trader.

The arbitrage between New York and London remained wide at 60 cents and traders said the level could narrow if the funds, long in New York but short in London decide to get out in New York and buy in London.
